claim: The Bujaco Tower rises above Plaza Mayor and its observation deck offers panoramic views of the square, the maze of Old Town streets, and other watchtowers like the Torre del Horno, making it the best photo spot.
quote: The observation deck at the top offers a panoramic view of Plaza Mayor, the labyrinth of narrow streets in the Old Town, and other watchtowers such as the Torre del Horno

claim: Bujaco Tower entry costs about €2.50 and opens Tuesday to Sunday, 10:00-14:00 and 17:00-20:00, with a small museum inside.
quote: Entry costs €2.50 and opening times are Tuesday to Sunday, 10:00 AM – 2:00 PM and 5:00 PM – 8:00 PM

claim: Plaza Mayor is the bustling heart of Cáceres, framed by the Bujaco Tower and Arco de la Estrella, the main gateway through which you step into the silent stone Old Town.
quote: Arco de la Estrella is the main gateway into the historic centre of Cáceres, with the busy Plaza Mayor on one side and a maze of cobbled streets and medieval buildings on the other

claim: The Concatedral de Santa María bell tower can be climbed for a panoramic view over the monumental city, especially fine at sunset.
quote: The Concatedral of Santa María offers a panoramic view of the Monumental City from the bell tower

claim: The Concatedral de Santa María bell tower has general admission of €4.00, reduced €3.50, and youth €3.00 for ages 12-18 or students up to 25.
quote: general admission at €4.00, reduced tickets at €3.50, and young tickets at €3.00 for those aged 12-18 or university students up to 25 years old

claim: The Old Jewish Quarter sits in the Barrio de San Antonio de la Quebrada southeast of the Old Town, a neighbourhood of narrow cobbled streets and whitewashed houses; the former synagogue is now the Ermita de San Antonio, and Stars of David appear on street signs and in the cobblestones.
quote: The Old Synagogue (now the Ermita de San Antonio) was the epicentre of Jewish life in the city of Cáceres... the Star of David can be found on each of the streets signs as well as on the ground, in black and white cobblestones

claim: An official Jewish Quarter route includes the Olivar de la Judería (a hidden garden park) and the Baluarte de los Pozos tourist centre, which exhibits the Jewish quarters of Extremadura and Portugal and includes the Los Pozos Tower.
quote: the "Baluarte de los Pozos" Tourist Centre, where you can see an exhibition of the Jewish Quarters of Extremadura and Portugal, and also visit the garden and the Los Pozos Tower

claim: Cáceres' Old Town doubled as King's Landing in both Game of Thrones and House of the Dragon; HotD filming sites include the street of La Amargura, the dome of the Toledo-Moctezuma palace, the Plaza de Conde de Canilleros, the Arco de la Estrella, and Plaza de Santa María.
quote: The street of La Amargura, the dome of the palace of Toledo-Moctezuma, the square of Conde de Canilleros and the archway called Arcos de la Estrella have been some of the filming locations of House of the Dragon

claim: Guided night tours of about 90 minutes recount legends, mysteries and curiosities of Cáceres, covering sites like Isabel de Moctezuma, the House of the Monkey, Mansaborah, the House of the Sun, and the Jewish quarter.
quote: official tours last approximately one and a half hours, and they cover points of interest including Isabel de Moctezuma, the house of the monkey, Mansaborah, the house of the sun, and the Jewish quarter

claim: The Torre de las Cigüeñas (Palacio de las Cigüeñas) on Plaza de San Mateo is named for the storks that nest on it and is the only Old Town tower that kept its battlements after Queen Isabella I's 1476 edict ordered them removed, surviving today as a 25m crenellated tower.
quote: Only the Torre de las Cigüeñas (Tower of the Storks, named for the birds that nest there) was saved and still survives today... majestic 25-meter tower... the only defensive structure in the city that has preserved its original height and crenelated top

claim: Cáceres' Old Town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site whose Renaissance palaces and churches are crowned by storks' nests, blending Roman, Islamic, Gothic and Italian Renaissance styles.
quote: Surrounded by mansions, Renaissance palaces and churches crowned by storks' nests, you'll understand why Cáceres is a World Heritage City

claim: The white twin-towered Baroque Iglesia de San Francisco Javier on Plaza de San Jorge can be climbed (about 100 steps, ~€1.50) for what many call the best panoramic views of the Old Town.
quote: The two towers can be visited and climbed to the bell tower, from where you can see what are probably the best views of the old town... an entry fee of only €1.50
